content.thinking:
I'm piecing together the postmortem timeline: ZeroDivisionError errors in spend_summary.py around 19:54-20:00 coincided with the account page error rate spike, and it looks like the P3 flag toggle combined with the P2 deploy that removed a guard is what triggered the failure.

Tracing the mechanism, revision 383534e removed the empty-month guard, so when average_spend_per_item_this_month ran against shoppers with no recorded purchases, it divided by zero — and since the flag P3 routed traffic to that path, the request boundary caught the exception and failed the whole page rather than a reading simply not being executed. I'm noting that while one source suggests the main branch uses a different filter field, the actual running revision filters by recorded_at, which makes empty lists more likely by excluding null-dated records.

Now I'm laying out the causal chain step by step: first, account pages failed for affected shoppers, grounded in the error and alert evidence; second, this happened because requests hit the unguarded division causing a ZeroDivisionError that the boundary converted into a page failure; third, I'm tracing back to why that started at 19:54, tied to the flag rollout timing.

I'm considering whether to rule out the earlier P1 deploy — checking the metrics window, since the read spans roughly 15:54 to 19:54 with a healthy 1.0% baseline error rate throughout, plus logs showing normal page renders between 19:24 and 19:47 while the flag was still off. That supports ruling out P1 as a cause, citing the metrics and log sources. As for the P2 deploy happening at the same time as P3, that can't be ruled out since it's part of the actual cause — the revert action only disabled the flag but left the deploy in place.

I should be careful here — a candidate pointed to the deploy as the cause, but the record shows no rollback occurred, so I'll phrase the ruled-out claim as "revision 383534e alone, with the flag off, broke the pages," ruled out by T10/T23/T25/T26. The flag history at T16 just confirms P3 as the single flag change by Argus, not ruling out anything else. Now I'm moving to why that path actually failed, looking at the monthly function.

At 383534e, the function divides total_this_month_cents by the count of purchases recorded this month with no guard for an empty list, so a shopper with no recorded purchases triggers a ZeroDivisionError, per S2, D1, G5309. Deploy P2 at 19:54 removed the guard clause while also changing the filter to use recorded_at, per P2 and D1. So the chain should run: the function lacks a guard, then why — P2 removed it while changing the filter, and the final step should state in one sentence why that change actually broke the service, leaving the deeper mechanism to the root cause.

Let me structure the chain: pages failed because requests hit a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which crashed the whole page at the boundary. Those requests reached the monthly-average path because the monthly-spend-feature flag flipped on at P3's instant, routing most traffic through render_spend_summary into average_spend_per_item_this_month. That function failed because the revision running on all replicas, deployed at P2's instant, had stripped out the empty-month guard.

I'm also checking whether the flag-to-code mapping is actually confirmed — the docstring in monthly_statement.py on main does state that monthly-spend-feature gates the statement panel, which supports the connection, though I should verify this isn't just incidental documentation versus the actual gating logic.

Looking at the code paths: render_monthly_statement for an empty month raises ValueError, but the logs show ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which is a different code path entirely. Since _the_figure_for runs before _the_statement_for, the ZeroDivisionError would surface first and prevent the ValueError from ever occurring, and the statement only renders when the period isn't None anyway — so I need to pin down exactly when the G5309 errors began relative to when the flag was flipped on.

Checking the timing, errors started at 19:54 right as the flag went on, and flipping it back off at T25-T26 confirmed recovery. The deployment only touched spend_summary.py, meaning the statement code stayed at its earlier version, so the flag being enabled is what routed requests into the spend_summary path where line 47 lives — now I'm trying to map that line number against the diff hunks to confirm it corresponds to the return statement near the end of the modified block.

I'm continuing to trace line numbers through the second function, average_spend_per_item_this_month, comparing the docstring content against the diff hunk headers to confirm the line offsets match between the two revisions.

I'm double-checking the diff's line numbering against the actual file at that commit—the docstring sits around line 47 while the division logic is around line 60, which seems like a mismatch worth flagging as potentially a deliberate inconsistency in how the scenario was generated, rather than something I'm misreading.

I'll attribute the error to the monthly division based on the flag correlation and S2, not on an unrun reading, so cause_rests_on_an_unrun_reading is false. I'll note the line-number mismatch as an assumption, but I'm wary about citing "spend_summary.py:47" verbatim since it contains a figure that could be misread as a labeled number rather than plain text.

I should mention the revision 383534e since those are fine to cite as given, and avoid repeating C1's "about 30%" figure. I'll note the flag rollout went from a partial share of evaluations to full "on" status over time, and that the error rate stays below 100% because only idle shoppers without purchases this month trigger the failure, peaking at 37.5%.

For contributing factors, I'll point out that no test or review appears to have caught the removal of the empty-month guard — the test file as it stood at that revision only had the helper for the no-purchase case but nothing exercising the monthly path with an empty month, so both new cases would raise against the current code.

I'm proposing a preventive item: add a CI check running the account-page tests with each rollout flag toggled on and off before deploy, since no safeguard existed to catch a regression like this before shipping.

Then I'm noting a second issue — the deploy and flag switch-on happened simultaneously, exposing all traffic at once rather than ramping gradually; the data shows 186 of 200 instances flipped on within the first minute, so there was no canary period to limit blast radius.

I propose splitting this into two process items: ramp flag rollouts gradually, and never switch a flag on in the same window as a deploy that changes the gated code. I'm also considering whether the request handler failing the entire page when a single figure errors (S1) is itself a contributing factor, even though another part of the system deliberately avoids swallowing errors — testing whether containing that failure would have shortened or stopped the incident regardless of root cause.

I'm weighing whether to propose rendering the page without the spend figure when it fails, but that seems to conflict with the stated design philosophy of showing a wrong number rather than an error, so I'll likely leave it out to avoid contradicting intentional choices.

Then there's the fact that nobody was paged — the alert never linked to an on-call incident. I'm checking whether this detection gap counts as a factor, since mitigation happened anyway through Argus, and whether a person being paged would have mattered given the rollback was unavailable.

I'm leaning toward putting "no one was paged" under went_wrong as its own finding, with an action item to link the HighErrorRate alert to an on-call page, since it's not clearly demonstrable that paging would have shortened the incident, so it doesn't rise to a contributing factor.

Separately, there's the issue that the rollback couldn't execute because the deployment platform's API returned a 503, leaving the faulty revision running — that's another went_wrong, pairing with an action item to investigate the platform's unavailability. Since the flag revert already fixed things, the rollback gap isn't itself a shortening factor, but it does leave the risk that if the flag is re-enabled, the same bug could resurface, which points toward a still_at_risk item.

I should add an action item here: before re-enabling monthly-spend-feature, the statement panel owner needs to decide whether an empty month should raise in render_monthly_statement, since that's how the ValueError was read. I'm also noting that F1's fix was written against main, which filters by in_current_month rather than recorded_at, so merging it wouldn't automatically carry over the recorded_at change — the actual fix revision would need to be deployed separately.

Separately, I'm flagging that revision 383534e9, the one that actually ran, isn't in main's history according to Code-Fix's reading of the repo. That raises a process question about why that revision exists outside main and whether reconciling it is something the owner needs to decide on.

For detection, the alert timing falls within accounted_for, so that's fine. On what went well: the Investigator read the deploy diff and logs and correctly named the ZeroDivisionError path as candidate C1, Argus moved to C2 when rollback failed, Mitigation reverted and confirmed the flag, and Code-Fix proposed a draft PR. And we got lucky that the fault sat behind a flag that could be toggled without touching the deployment platform itself.

I'm noting that the faulty code was gated by a flag Argus could switch off through the flag provider even while the deployment platform was unreachable, which is why the pages recovered without a rollback — a bit of a coincidence. I'm also flagging assumptions: a line number mismatch, and that use_monthly_summary was set by the monthly-spend feature, inferred from timing and the confirmed revert rather than a direct mapping row, though F1's docstring note supports it. For cause_in_plain_words, I'm framing it as: a code change removed a check for shoppers who hadn't bought anything that month.

Working on the root cause phrasing, I'm describing revision 383534e as removing the guard that returned an empty result when a shopper had no purchases that month, changing the logic to only count purchases recorded in the current month — so for shoppers with none, it divides by an empty list's length and raises a ZeroDivisionError, which the account page then surfaces as a failure. I need to avoid using any number words, so I'm substituting the placeholder value instead of writing "zero" directly.

For the symptom line, I'm simplifying to "Account pages failed for some shoppers" to stay under the word limit without implying causation. I'm also noting that the deploy alone can't be ruled out independently from the flag flip since both happened at 19:54 — I'll need to use the post-revert logs to separate their effects, citing the relevant metrics and logs for the ruled-out hypothesis.

For action items, I'm drafting a prevention measure: add CI tests that run the account page with each rollout flag enabled, specifically covering an account with no purchases this month, so future changes behind a flag get tested on that exact path.

Then process items: investigate how 383534e got deployed outside main's review path, ramp flag rollouts incrementally with error-rate checks between stages, and avoid flipping a flag on in the same window as a deploy that changes gated code — hold until the deploy is confirmed healthy. For mitigation, I'm noting deploying a fixed revision to io-shop in place of 383534e once merged, plus deciding on the ValueError before re-enabling the flag, and ensuring on-call gets paged for HighErrorRate on io-shop.

Now checking why the deployment platform API returned 503, since that blocked rollback availability. Looking at CF-2 as a contributing factor: evidence shows 186 of 200 instances flipped on in the first minute, so a ramped rollout would have caught the error rise on a smaller slice — and since it coincided with the deploy, the investigator couldn't isolate the two changes. I'm also flagging that the rollback attempt on 383534e couldn't complete due to the platform's 503 response, which is worth including as something that went wrong, separate from the fault itself.

Now compiling the went_well items by actor: the Investigator Agent reading the deploy diff that revealed the guard's removal, Argus pivoting to the flag candidate once rollback failed, the Mitigation Agent disabling monthly-spend-feature as a reversible action, and confirming the revert once the service metrics left the incident's level.

"The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for review," skipping the specific PR number since it reads more like an identifier than a label worth including verbatim.

action_items.item: Make CI run the account-page tests with each rollout flag switched on, including an account with past purchases but none this month, so that a change to code behind a flag is tested on the path the flag selects.
Find out how revision 383534e came to be deployed to production when Code-Fix found it not in main's history, and whether it passed review.
Ramp io-shop feature flags up in steps, checking the error rate between steps, instead of switching them on for most traffic at once.
Do not switch on a flag in the same minute as a deploy that changes the code it gates: wait until the deploy is seen healthy with the flag off.
Once the fix is merged, deploy a revision carrying it to io-shop in place of revision 383534e. The recorded_at change in 383534e is not in main, so its owner must decide whether it ships.

Before monthly-spend-feature is switched back on, have the statement panel's owner decide whether render_monthly_statement should still raise for an empty month. Code-Fix read it as raising ValueError there and found the flag named as gating that panel.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is brought in.
Find out why the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, and restore it so that rollbacks of io-shop can be done.

causal_chain.step: Some shoppers' account page requests failed. Account-page error warnings rose above their usual level, and the error rate the alert watches (the share of all the service's requests answered with a server error) stayed above its threshold until the alert fired.

Those requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The account page's request boundary catches any exception and returns a failed page, so the whole page failed and not just one figure.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee at {P1.1}: the metrics read across the hours before the onset show the service at its usual error rate with that revision in place. Account pages were logged rendering normally, and the flag was logged off, up to the onset.

Revision 383534e, deployed at {P2.1}, breaking pages without the flag: after the flag was switched off, the service left the incident's level and the revert was confirmed. The rollback of that revision was never done, so it was still running when the service recovered.

causal_chain.step: Requests reached the monthly spend average in spend_summary.py because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P3.1}. From {G971b.6} most of the flag's evaluations came back on, and from {Gce95.4} every evaluation logged was on. When a request's monthly-summary rollout decision is on, render_spend_summary sends it to average_spend_per_item_this_month.

The monthly average failed for shoppers with no purchase recorded this month because revision 383534e had removed its empty-month guard. That revision was deployed at {P2.1}, and at {T10.1} it was running on every replica.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change removed the step that handled shoppers who had bought nothing this month, and when a new feature that uses that code was switched on, the account page failed for those shoppers.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that caught the removal of the empty-month guard before revision 383534e was deployed. By Code-Fix's reading of the test file, no existing test ran the monthly path for an account with past purchases but none this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test running the monthly path for a shopper with no purchases this month would have failed on that revision, and it would not have reached production in that form.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was switched on for most traffic at once, at the same instant as the deploy that changed the code it gates, with no gradual ramp seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Exposing the new code to a small slice first would have limited the failures to that slice and shown the error rise before most shoppers were reached.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: The faulty code was reached only through a flag, which Argus could switch off through the flag provider while the deployment platform was unreachable. The pages recovered without a rollback.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the diff of the deploy that landed at the onset, which shows the empty-month guard removed.
Argus moved on to the flag candidate C2 when the rollback for C1 could not be done.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off. The action can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent watched the service leave the incident's level and judged the revert confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so no person was brought in, even when the rollback could not be done.
The rollback of revision 383534e could not be done because the deployment platform's API answered {T19.2}, so the revision without the guard was left running.

input.root_cause: Revision 383534e removed from average_spend_per_item_this_month the guard that returned {D1.1} for a shopper who had bought nothing this month, and changed it to count only purchases whose recorded_at falls in the current month. For any shopper with no such purchase, it now floor-divides total_this_month_cents by the length of an empty list and raises ZeroDivisionError. The account page's request boundary catches that error and fails the whole page.
input.still_at_risk: While revision 383534e stays running, switching monthly-spend-feature back on would fail account pages again for shoppers with no purchase recorded this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
